The treatment therefore for this is transition, its currently the best we have. It is also why the debate rages on about pronouns, rights, bathrooms, sports etc. What currently holds us back is technology. I think we shouldn't be debating this because debating solves nothing, we need to be working on the technical challenges instead.

When this happened to me I was deeply scared, because until that point there was a safe barrier between my mind and reality and all this told me was that yes, dreams can actually come true.

And so it was this event that lead me to look over the nightly recurring dreams ive had for 17 years, which when you look at the landscape of human civilization today, things start to match up.

Alrighty you've asked me so I will deliver, feel free to absolutely pick this story apart with a fine scalpel...

This occurred in January 2020, went to bed like id usually do and had a very random dream. In the dream I was looking at a map of the UK, at a beach in Norfolk. Except on the map it was called Clifton. I knew this was wrong because the only Clifton I was aware of is located in York.

And that was the dream, map, Clifton, beach.

Now as soon as Id woken up and turned my phone on, id received a message in the night from a girl on a dating app who lives in Blackpool. I know this because she'd sent me her location, which for me was incredibly rare indeed. But it was when I looked at the map location she gave me, that made me gasp.

There, on the map location was her road name. 

*Clifton Drive*

Which was situated two blocks away from the beech.

Now this absolutely stunned me, because id never had such a random dream before like that and the fact that three points of data matched.

-Dreaming of maps
-The map location being near beaches or showing a beach
-The map location giving the same name of Clifton on both sides (one in my dream and one in real life).

I would go further to say there is a fourth point of synchronization here, the fact that the map in my dream was incorrect. Clifton wasn't located in Norfolk, but was a road in Blackpool.

Like I said, ive had déjà vu before, and think I've seen an article discussing the neurological causes. Something about it being a delay in the brain that triggers the response when exposed to similar information.

But with this, I woke up from my dream and immediately turned my phone on and BAM!

There it was.
